title: Forensics audit ontology: change log and migration plan
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a focused migration playbook for the audit/event schema and the event ontology used for forensics, SIEM exports, and evidence automation. It is intended for engineering owners (ingest/exporters), SRE, security product, and compliance reviewers. The goal is to stage a backward-compatible evolution that enables RBAC v2 attributes, richer actor/actor_context fields, and explicit evidence pointers while minimizing breakage for downstream SIEM consumers and archived analytics.

High-level summary of changes (what and why):
- Introduce "actor_role" and "actor_scope" as first-class indexed fields to support RBAC v2 queries without full payload inspection. Rationale: SIEM queries and quick incident response must be able to filter by role (e.g., admin, service-account) and scope (org/project).
- Add "evidence_refs" array (list of URIs) that point to immutable evidence bundles (S3/GCS + signed manifest) rather than embedding bulky payloads in the event. Rationale: reduces event size and centralizes evidence retention policies.
- Split existing "resource" field into typed fields: "resource_type", "resource_id", "resource_namespace" to make indexing predictable across services.
- Mark "event_version" at the top level and adopt semver-like change tags (major.minor.patch) for audit events. Rationale: consumers can route parsing logic by event_version.
- Optional field "confidence_score" for automated detection events to support triage automation and thresholding.

Event taxonomy mapping notes (legacy -> staged ontology):
- legacy: {actor: {id, name}, action, resource, ts, meta}  --> staged: {actor_id, actor_name, actor_role, actor_scope, action, resource_type, resource_id, resource_namespace, event_version, timestamp, evidence_refs, meta}
- action: keep existing verbs but add an "action_class" tag (data_access, config_change, auth, system) to allow coarse-grained dashboards.
- meta: keep as free-form JSON blob but avoid storing PII. Encourage use of "meta.summary" short text.

Sample event (staged format, illustrative only):
{
  "event_version": "2.0.0",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-10T14:23:05Z",
  "action": "grant-role",
  "action_class": "config_change",
  "actor_id": "svc-1234",
  "actor_name": "billing-sync",
  "actor_role": "service-account",
  "actor_scope": "org:redwood:proj:billing",
  "resource_type": "iam_role",
  "resource_id": "role-internal-admin",
  "resource_namespace": "org:redwood",
  "evidence_refs": ["s3://redwood-audit-evidence/2026/01/10/evt-9876/manifest.json"],
  "confidence_score": "",
  "meta.summary": "automated grant via terraform apply (plan #764)",
  "meta.linked_pr": "https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/764"
}

Compatibility and versioning policy (operational rules):
- event_version MAJOR bump indicates breaking change (field rename/removal or semantic meaning change). Consumers must fail-fast or use translation layer.
- event_version MINOR bump indicates additive fields or new optional enums; old consumers should ignore unknown fields.
- event_version PATCH for documentation / annotation only.
- Migration rule: emit both legacy-compatible wrapper events for 60 days after switching producers, then flip to native only once downstream consumers have certified (see certification checklist below).

Migration plan (timeline + owner tasks):
Phase 0 - Preparation (2 weeks):
- Owners: security-eng (schema design), infra (exporter changes), product (comms).
- Deliverable: proposed schema v2.0 documented and sample payloads.
- Blacklist: do not change storage retention policy during this window.

Phase 1 - Dual-write (30 days):
- Implement dual-write at source: produce both legacy event (event_version: 1.x) and staged v2.0 event for every auditable action.
- Infra action: flag on exporter to add actor_role/actor_scope where available; populate from RBAC v2 lookup service.
- Telemetry: add metric audit.events.v2_emitted and audit.events.legacy_emitted.

Phase 2 - Consumer onboarding and certification (30–45 days):
- Downstream teams (SIEM, analytics, evidence-processor) must run their ingestion tools in parallel and report parity metrics (field presence, rate, and schema errors).
- Security to run automated validation harness that asserts required fields for incident use-cases.

Phase 3 - Cutover & cleanup (14 days):
- If parity is >= 99.5% and no critical parsing issues, schedule cutover window. Switch exporter to single-write v2.0.
- After 60 days post-cutover, remove legacy event production.

Rollback guidance (if cutover causes breakage):
- Re-enable dual-write toggle and surface the legacy feed. Alert downstream owners and revert rolling deploys of any consumer change if necessary.
- Keep a snapshot of v2.0 payloads for forensic debugging during rollback.

SIEM export considerations: 
- Field mapping: ensure resource_type and resource_namespace are populated as keyword fields in SIEM index mapping; actor_role and actor_scope should be searchable tokens.
- Size and retention: evidence_refs must be treated as pointers; SIEM exports should not dereference these at ingest time to avoid huge indices. If a SIEM analyst needs content, provide a secure UI to fetch evidence bundles with access checks.
- Alerting: adopt action_class into alert rules (e.g., generate high-severity alert for config_change by admin role outside business hours).

RBAC v2 interactions and constraints:
- For any event where actor is a service account, populate actor_role = "service-account" and attach actor_scope from the RBAC lookup table. If lookup fails, emit actor_role = "unknown-role" and include lookup_error in meta.
- Some legacy systems cannot expose role metadata; build best-effort enrichment (async job that backfills actor_role) and flag in parity metrics.

Evidence automation hooks and retention model: 
- evidence_refs should reference a signed manifest that contains checksum, size, content_type, and retention_expiry. The manifest must be immutable once created.
- The evidence-archiver process will enforce retention_expiry and produce a compact retention-audit event to the same audit topic.

Testing & validation checklist (must pass before cutover):
- Schema conformance tests (producer unit tests + integration tests).
- End-to-end parity test: ensure every legacy field consumed by analytics has a mapped v2 equivalent or a documented fallback.
- SIEM ingestion dry-run: sample index with mapped fields and confirm cardinality expectations.
- RBAC enrichment smoke test: 95% coverage for high-frequency actors.

Operational runbook snippets (quick steps):
- If SIEM parser throws unknown-field errors, switch parser to permissive mode (accept unknowns) and open a ticket to fix mapping.
- If evidence_refs are inaccessible after cutover, run evidence-archiver health checks: check S3 permissions, manifest signatures, and the archiver queue.

Open questions / risks: 
- Long-term: do we want a separate stream for large evidence artifacts vs. inline audit events? Could simplify SIEM but complicate correlation windows.
- Risk: slower producers while fetching RBAC v2 metadata synchronous; mitigation: async enrichment and dual-write.
- Risk: downstream analytics jobs that JOIN on previous monolithic resource field will need rewrites. Provide translation shim in the ingestion layer.

Appendix: migration parity checklist (short):
- [ ] Dual-write enabled for all producers
- [ ] telemetry metrics show v2 emissions at 100%
- [ ] SIEM sample index created and verified
- [ ] RBAC enrichment coverage >=95% for top-100 actors
- [ ] Evidence manifests visible and signed
- [ ] Downstream teams certified in Confluence (links in linked_artifacts)

Notes to reviewers: please comment inline on fields you think should be required versus optional. If you own a downstream consumer, add a short paragraph about your acceptance criteria and a preferred cutover window in the Confluence linked above.
